goal: fw show given a landed commit SHA renders that commit's producing run detail by reading its Flywheel-Run trailer, and exits non-zero naming the commit un-attributed when no such trailer is present.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- _cmd_show and its run-or-task-id resolution; module is over 800 lines, use serena symbols
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_history.py -- collect_run_detail / RunDetail, the renderer the lookup reuses unchanged
packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- read-only: the shared trailer key constants the prerequisite task exported; resolve the value via git, do not re-derive the vocabulary
constraints: Resolution is git-truth: read the Flywheel-Run trailer from the commit object in the repository; no new store columns, tables, or indexes
Existing fw show behavior for run ids and task ids is byte-identical; SHA handling only engages when the argument resolves to a commit object and not to a known run or task
An un-attributed commit (no Flywheel-Run trailer) is a hard non-zero exit naming the commit -- never a fuzzy fallback to a nearby run
Commit the change (Conventional Commits) before reporting done
non_goals: Do not add a new CLI verb; this extends the argument resolution of the existing show verb
Do not modify the stamping engine or either submit strategy
Do not weaken, delete, or modify existing assertions in the pinned test files
Do not read or write under .flywheel/verification/
edge_cases: A commit whose Flywheel-Run trailer names a run absent from the store exits non-zero naming the missing run id -- distinct from the un-attributed message
An argument that is neither a known run id, task id, nor resolvable commit keeps today's error behavior
The rendered detail for a SHA is the same run-detail view fw show renders for the run id itself, including the landed line
